purpose: Apalutamide is used to treat prostate cancer. It is used specifically in men whose prostate cancer has not yet spread to other parts of the body but is no longer responding well to standard hormone therapy, or in men whose cancer has spread and who are also receiving other hormone-lowering treatment.
how_it_works: Prostate cancer cells need the male hormone testosterone to grow and spread. Apalutamide works by blocking the places on cancer cells where testosterone would normally attach and signal the cancer to grow. By blocking these signals, it helps slow down or stop the cancer from growing.
common_side_effects: Feeling tired or weak, joint pain, rash on the skin, hot flashes, decreased appetite, weight loss, high blood pressure, diarrhea, nausea, and falls or fractures. Some men may also notice changes in their cholesterol or thyroid levels on blood tests.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious skin rashes — call your doctor right away if you develop a widespread rash. It can increase your risk of falls, broken bones, and seizures. It may also cause heart problems. This drug can harm an unborn baby, so men taking it must use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 3 months after the last dose. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as apalutamide can interact with many common drugs by affecting how they are processed in your body.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is four 60 mg tablets taken together once a day, making a total dose of 240 mg. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day. Swallow the tablets whole — do not crush or chew them.
